abstract: Single-cell genomics has transformed the study of cellular diversity, but the resulting atlases are scattered across publications, formats, and annotation standards. Efforts to make these data findable and interoperable have focused largely on aggregating and harmonizing existing model organism datasets. The Biodiversity Cell Atlas database is an open resource that addresses this gap by uniformly (re)processing, curating, and comparing whole-organism single-cell atlases sampled across the eukaryotic tree of life. Starting from raw sequencing data, each dataset is processed through a consistent workflow and enriched with standardized quality-control metrics, metacell-level aggregation, gene co-expression modules, and phylogeny-based orthology and functional annotation, enabling both gene- and cell type-centric exploration within species as well as principled comparisons between them. The portal currently hosts 39 datasets across 33 species spanning 13 eukaryotic phyla, and offers multiple levels of access, from raw and filtered count matrices to normalized, aggregated, and analysis-ready data layers. These are accessible through an interactive web interface (https://portal.biodiversitycellatlas.org) and a documented REST API (https://portal.biodiversitycellatlas.org/api/v1/). All data, code, and infrastructure are continuously released and maintained under open licenses, providing a curated and reusable foundation for comparative single-cell genomics.
